body: @cebe but it is not only for postgresql, so any data types with precisions are broken now, no?

they are broken after @qiangxue fix but that has been reverted. The only thing that is not working is adding precision to types where yii does not know that the dbms supports precision. these are for example postgres timestamp types, not sure if there are more.

if you specify  'string' and your dbms does have precision for it, yii will transform this to 'string(123)' where 123 will be the default precision of the system.

if you specify  'string(100)' and your dbms does **not** have precision support, yii will transform this to 'string'.
currently i dont see any checks for precision support for different dbms, i guess it should be done in `getColumnType` of each dbms `QueryBuilder` .

check the tests: https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/master/tests/unit/framework/db/QueryBuilderTest.php#L45 it is already implemented and it works.

docs: https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/master/framework/db/QueryBuilder.php#L578
@cebe the fix is incorrect as you may know try `timestamp(4)` as an use-case . As i said it is a question of parsing bug that @qiangxue was fixing .
I do not get what the problem is, just created a test case that uses timestamp(4) and it creates a column in pgsql with the precision.
just tried it now , all is correct , thanks .
